title: Product with the invertible interval projects by a categorical equivalence
statement: Use small simplicial sets, degreewise products, nerves and quasicategories from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and categorical equivalences in the test-functor convention of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $\mathcal I$ be the ordinary groupoid with objects $0,1$ and exactly one morphism between each ordered pair, and put $I=N(\mathcal I)$. For every small simplicial set $R$, the projection $\pi_R:R\times I\to R$ is a categorical equivalence. No quasicategory, nonemptiness or finiteness hypothesis on $R$ is required; the assertion holds in every input universe.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.4, printed p.92: categorical equivalences are preserved by products; the contractible groupoid interval supplies the other factor. Agent-extracted auxiliary assertion from the original proof step 3 of lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison, within Proposition 4.2.1.5. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: An $n$-simplex of $I$ is uniquely specified by a string $(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$ of objects in $\{0,1\}$: all arrows between successive objects are unique. A simplicial operator selects or repeats entries. Define $\mu:I\times I\to I$ by sending strings $(a_j)_j,(t_j)_j$ to $(b_j)_j$, where $b_j=0$ if $t_j=0$ and $b_j=a_j$ if $t_j=1$. This commutes with every selection or repetition of entries, so is a simplicial map. For the constant endpoint strings, $\mu(a,0)=0$ and $\mu(a,1)=a$. Set $X=R\times I$ and let $s:R\to X$ insert the constant $0$ string. Then $\pi_Rs=1_R$, while $((r,a),t)\mapsto(r,\mu(a,t))$ is a simplicial map $X\times I\to X$ with endpoints $s\pi_R$ and $1_X$. These are explicit degreewise identities, without a condition on $R$.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.4, printed p.92, specialized to the invertible interval; explicit agent proof by its contraction. Proposition 1.2.7.3 and Proposition 2.2.5.8 supply the functor-category interpretation. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED.

proof.text: Fix a quasicategory $C$ in any sufficiently large universe, and put $E=\operatorname{Fun}(R,C)$ and $D=\operatorname{Fun}(X,C)$. The first assertion of [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test], applied to $u=\pi_R:X\to R$, says that $D$ and $E$ are quasicategories; its domain need only be a small simplicial set. Precomposition defines $P=\pi_R^*:E\to D$ and $Q=s^*:D\to E$. In degree $n$ these send a map to its composite with $\pi_R\times1_{\Delta^n}$ or $s\times1_{\Delta^n}$, respectively. Thus $QP=1_E$ strictly, and $PQ$ sends $F:X\times\Delta^n\to C$ to $F\circ(s\pi_R\times1_{\Delta^n})$.

source.place: Theorem 3.6.8(ii)-(iii), printed pp.115-116, and Remark 3.6.5, printed p.114; read online 2026-10-17. Applied through the existing lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test; the interval contraction and its triangle witnesses are the explicit agent construction here. Archive WANTED.

proof.text: Construct $K:D\times I\to D$ on an $n$-simplex $(F,t)$, with $F:X\times\Delta^n\to C$ and $t:\Delta^n\to I$, by $K(F,t)=F\circ\kappa_t$. On an $m$-simplex $((r,a),\beta)$ of $X\times\Delta^n$, where $\beta:[m]\to[n]$, put $$\kappa_t((r,a),\beta)=((r,\mu(a,t\beta)),\beta).$$ Here $t\beta$ is the restriction of the string $t$ along $\beta$, and $\mu$ is step 1's degreewise formula. Restricting along $\gamma:[l]\to[m]$ replaces $a$ by $a\gamma$ and $t\beta$ by $t\beta\gamma$; step 1's formula gives $\mu(a,t\beta)\gamma=\mu(a\gamma,t\beta\gamma)$. Hence $\kappa_t$ is a simplicial map, and restriction of $(F,t)$ along $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ gives exactly the restriction of $K(F,t)$ along $\alpha$. This verifies that $K$ itself is simplicial. Its endpoints are $PQ$ at $0$ and $1_D$ at $1$. Currying gives $\widetilde K:I\to\operatorname{Fun}(D,D)$: an $n$-simplex $t$ is sent to $K\circ(1_D\times t):D\times\Delta^n\to D$.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.4, printed p.92, specialized to the invertible interval; explicit agent proof by its contraction. Proposition 1.2.7.3 and Proposition 2.2.5.8 supply the functor-category interpretation. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED.

proof.text: The two edges $0\to1$ and $1\to0$ in $I$ and its two $2$-simplices with vertex strings $(0,1,0)$ and $(1,0,1)$ have long edges the degenerate edges at $0$ and $1$. Their images under $\widetilde K$ therefore give an edge $PQ\to1_D$, its reverse, and both inverse-triangle witnesses in $\operatorname{Fun}(D,D)$. By the definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], this is a coherent natural equivalence $PQ\simeq1_D$. Together with the strict equality $QP=1_E$ (whose degenerate edges and triangles supply the other natural equivalence), it makes the specified map $P=\pi_R^*$ a coherent functor equivalence with quasi-inverse $Q$. This holds for every test $C$. Condition (ii) implies condition (iii) in [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test], so $h(\pi_R^*)$ is an ordinary equivalence for every $C$. This is precisely the categorical-equivalence convention of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. All products and strings stay small in the input universe; tests and their functor objects may be taken in any larger universe. If $R=\varnothing$, both $D$ and $E$ are the one-point functor simplicial set and the same formulas apply; no vertex of $R$, horn filler of $R$, or finiteness assumption was used.
